title: Entanglement Scaling and Full Counting Statistics in Excited States of Two-Dimensional Rotating Fermions
authors: Priyangshu Goswami, Abhishek Dhar, Satya N. Majumdar, Anupam Kundu
abstract: We investigate the entanglement entropy of a class of $N$-particle excited state of fermions confined in a two-dimensional harmonic trap rotating at an angular frequency $Ω$. The excited state is constructed by filling a particular set of $N$ single-particle energy levels. We analytically compute the Rényi entropies of order $q$ in a disc of radius $r$ around the centre of the trap, and the cumulants corresponding to number fluctuations of fermions within the disc. We found that the area law scaling of entanglement entropy holds even for a class of excited states. We also verified the well-known series expansion of entanglement entropy in terms of the particle number cumulants for non-interacting fermions. We further derive the centered cumulant generating function, demonstrating that the associated probability distribution function in the disc has identical scaling properties, up to a variable shift, to the known ground-state result. Finally, we extend our result to an annular region, showing that both the Rényi entropy and particle number cumulants of the annulus decompose into sums of the corresponding quantities of the two bounding discs. These additive relations hold as long as the width of the annulus is sufficiently large.
summary: This work analytically computes the entanglement entropy and full counting statistics for non-interacting fermions in an excited state within a rotating 2D harmonic trap. The authors demonstrate that fundamental scaling laws, such as the area law, remain valid even for these highly excited states. Furthermore, they establish robust additive relations for both entropy and particle number cumulants when analyzing annular subsystems.
main_problem: The study investigates entanglement entropy (EE) and Full Counting Statistics (FCS) for excited states of fermions confined in a rotating trap, specifically testing the validity of area law scaling.
main_result: The area law scaling holds for EE even in these excited states, and both EE and particle number cumulants exhibit robust additive relations when calculated for an annular region.
method: Analytical computation using the overlap matrix formalism, which relates EE and FCS to eigenvalues of correlation matrices derived from non-interacting fermion wavefunctions.
model_or_system: Non-interacting spinless fermions confined in a two-dimensional harmonic trap rotating at an angular frequency $\Omega$. The system is analyzed for excited states constructed by filling consecutive single-particle energy levels (e.g., LLL sector).
key_observables: Rényi entanglement entropy ($S_q$), particle number cumulants ($\langle\hat{N}_D^pangle_c$), and the centered cumulant generating function.
important_parameters: The angular frequency $\Omega$, the radius $r$ (for discs), and the width of the annulus; analysis is performed in limits where the system size ($M, N$) is large.
main_assumptions: The fermions are non-interacting. Additivity for annular regions requires the width to be sufficiently large. The calculations often rely on asymptotic approximations derived from integral representations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate density profiles and show scaling behavior of Rényi entropy ($S(2)/\sqrt{N}$) across different regimes (inner edge, bulk, outer edge) in rescaled coordinates $\xi$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the formalism for EE and FCS using correlation matrices. It then calculates these quantities for discs, confirming area law scaling. Subsequently, it extends the analysis to annular regions, demonstrating additive decomposition of both entropy and cumulants.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous theoretical confirmation that fundamental scaling laws (like the area law) persist in complex excited states beyond the ground state, linking entanglement structure directly to particle number fluctuations in a controlled quantum setting.
